title: Guided Demo: Observing a Live XMPP Wire Protocol Session Transcript
solutionExplanation:
The demonstration module boots sample_xmpp_c2s (an OTP gen_statem process) on an ephemeral TCP port and runs bf_xmpp_c2s_harness to execute the five sequential state transitions required by RFC 6120:
1. wait_for_stream: Accepts the initial stream open and advertises SASL PLAIN authentication mechanisms.
2. wait_for_sasl: Receives credentials and responds with <success/>.
3. authenticated: Receives the client's IQ bind request and assigns the bound Full JID alice@localhost/obsidian.
4. session_established: Accepts incoming chat messages and acknowledges delivery.
5. Harness verification: Inspects the latency and protocol structure of each wire transition.

mentalModelCheck.question: Why does the XMPP C2S protocol keep a single TCP connection open persistently rather than using short-lived HTTP requests for each chat message?

options.label: To allow the server to push incoming stanzas to the client in real time with sub-millisecond latency without polling overhead.
options.explanation: XMPP maintains a long-lived bidirectional XML stream over a single TCP socket so either peer can push stanzas instantaneously.

options.label: Because XML documents can only be transmitted over raw TCP sockets.
options.explanation: XML can be sent over any transport, but persistent streaming avoids connection renegotiation latency.

options.label: Because Erlang processes cannot handle HTTP requests.
options.explanation: Erlang handles HTTP effortlessly (e.g. Cowboy), but real-time messaging requires low-latency bidirectional push streams.

options.label: Because SASL PLAIN authentication only works on raw sockets.
options.explanation: SASL PLAIN is transport-independent; persistent connections are chosen for real-time delivery.
